desc:
This binary search tree may contain duplicate values. For every node, all values in its left subtree are less than or equal to the node's value and all values in its right subtree are greater than or equal to it.

Return every value that occurs the maximum number of times in the tree, sorted in ascending order. Try to avoid a hash map: the BST order already groups equal values together.

Tree encoding. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level order. The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn, level by level, from left to right. A missing child is written as -1 (node values are never negative, so -1 cannot be confused with a value). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped. The empty tree is [].

For example, [5,2,7,-1,3,6] is the tree whose root 5 has left child 2 and right child 7; node 2 has no left child and right child 3; node 7 has left child 6 and no right child.

Example 1

tree = [1,-1,2,2]
Output: [2]
1 occurs once and 2 occurs twice.

Example 2

tree = [4,2,6,2,4,-1,6]
Output: [2,4,6]
The values in order are 2,2,4,4,6,6: three values tie with two occurrences each.
constraints: 0 ≤ node value ≤ 100,000; values may repeat; the tree satisfies the ordering rule above
hints: A hash map of counts, then picking all values with the largest count, solves it. What does the inorder sequence of a BST look like?
In the inorder sequence equal values sit next to each other, so each value forms one run.
Traverse inorder, track the length of the current run and the best run length so far. A longer run replaces the answer list; an equal-length run is appended to it.
editorial: Because an inorder traversal of such a tree is non-decreasing, all copies of a value appear consecutively. Walk the tree inorder (with an explicit stack to avoid deep recursion) and maintain the current value, the length of its run, the best run length seen so far and the list of values that reached it.

When a run becomes longer than the best length, reset the list to just this value. When it becomes exactly as long, append the value. Since each run grows one step at a time, a value is appended at most once, and the list comes out already sorted. Time is O(n); extra memory is O(h) for the stack, plus the answer.
